key_insight: Point2Part reframes 3D part decomposition as a joint partitioning problem: predict all parts together so they are non-overlapping and fully cover the original shape. This makes the decomposition more consistent and usable for downstream part-level tasks.
problem_solved: Existing 3D part decomposition methods can produce overlapping parts or leave gaps, which breaks the idea of a complete, clean partition of the object. This paper addresses the need for decompositions that exactly cover the shape without overlap.
method: Formulates part decomposition as unified 3D partitioning rather than independent part prediction.
Uses point prompts to guide the model toward desired parts.
Predicts all parts jointly so the final output is a complete, non-overlapping partition of the full shape.
impact: This matters because many downstream 3D applications need clean part-level representations for editing, analysis, and interaction. A partitioned output is more reliable for robotics, CAD, and scene understanding workflows.
visual_elements: Side-by-side comparison of overlapping/gapped parts vs. exact partitioning

paper_title: Point2Part: Unified 3D Partitioning from Point Prompts
paper_authors: Hao-Tang Tsui, Yu-Rou Tuan, Xiaoxuan Ma, Nicolas Ugrinovic, Takaaki Shiratori
